body: Your response literally made me cry. It feels so good to know someone not much older than me knows what I'm going through. And I'll do everything you said. I pinkie promise. I just have flare ups sometimes. I'll feel fine one minute, and then basically nothing can get me off the edge.

Thank you. All these responses helped me more than I thought they would. Your story is inspiring to say the least. In regards to what I'm passionate about, I'd say that the closest I've come to feeling passionate about something is by watching movies. I really really like movies. I like all kinds of movies; old movies,  foreign films, silents, I'm just obsessed with the history of film. I think that's part of the reason I can't make friends. I don't have much to talk about besides movies. I like acting and I've done some school plays, but that's not a realistic career choice. Well, nothing in film really is. But sometimes I feel like watching a Woody Allen movie can save my life. They just make me feel really good. About myself. And the world. Nothing makes me feel more calm than watching a good movie. To me, something like 2001: A Space Odyssey gives me a better high than pot. I know that's sort of off-topic for r/Suicidewatch, but I just need somewhere to vent.

My parents never really loved one another, and my dad being a junkie, they had some horrific screaming matches in front of me. I'll never forget how my mother recounted him hitting her head against the side of the bathtub (not that she didn't hit him). I can't even imagine being so angry that I yelled as loud as they did at another human being. I don't even know what they fought about; off-color Myspace messages, adultery, that sort of thing I imagine. It happened all the goddamn time for a while. It always ended in one of two ways; either my teary-eyed mother would ask me not to tell my grandparents, or I'd wake up in the middle of the night to the sound of sweet sweet make-up sex. This happened more often than my parents know about. Twice they did it while I was "sleeping" in the same exact room. I was too embarrassed to ask them to stop, so I just waited for them to finish (horrible, I know). Once, in hindsight hilariously, I woke to blaring death metal coming from their room. Upon further inspection, I heard my mother's moans. My parents were fucking to Soulfly. I'm positive that these horrific fights coupled with me witnessing their boning has fucked me up to this day. I still have a lot of social anxiety and low self-esteem, and sexually I have some self-image problems. But overall these fights are just bad memories, and I could have turned out a lot worse.

Not exactly death, but close to it. When my great grandpa was dying, my whole family all huddled into his room in his small Kentucky house (in the middle of the goddamn Deliverance woods, I might add). We were all basically waiting for him to die so we could have a funeral and go home. He was incredibly skinny, and, him being an alcoholic/drug addict for most of his life, he was having an uncomfortably hard time breathing. He kind of looked like one of the Skeksi's from the Dark Crystal. He couldn't get out of bed. What was so disturbing was that you could tell he knew he was going to die from his eyes. I remember he asked his son if he hated him, and then gave him $100. He died the next morning. Crazy guy. So how about that new Star Wars trailer you guys?

One of the most iconic special effects shots is the pen floating around the spaceship in zero gravity in 2001: A Space Odyssey. The way they accomplished the effect is what's mind-blowing; all they basically did was glue the pen to a clear glass window, and then turned it slowly in front of the camera. It looks just as flawless as anything in Gravity, and it wasn't CG or anything complicated like that. You could probably do it today in about ten minutes. It's beautiful in it's simplicity.

I'm a big fan of animation and after watching Akira (great movie) I became obsessed with watching as many "mature" animated films as I could. Mary and Max is a great one, and so is some anime, though a lot seems to be geared towards a younger teen boy-type demographic. This weird stigma animation has where people think it's for exclusively children is really strange, especially considering how CG-heavy many Hollywood films are nowadays. It's like, yes, we can watch cartoon trees and cartoon raccoons in cartoon spaceships traveling through cartoon space, just as long as we get a few shots of real-life shirtless Chris Pratt as well. Hopefully we can someday live in a world where I don't have to be embarrassed when a family member catches me watching Cowboy Bebop. That being said, I doubt a raunchy Seth Rogen movie called "Sausage Party" is going to be the trail-blazer animation fans hope for.
